subject: Reasoning
description: Step-wise rearrangements with two-rule alternation, position tracking

questions.stem: Input: 81 coin 64 dice 49 lock 36 ring. The machine's Step I moves the LARGEST number to the leftmost position. Step I will be:
questions.explanation: Largest number is 81; already at the leftmost position → Step I leaves it unchanged. Step II would move next-largest 64 to leftmost-but-one (after 81), etc. Distractor 1 swaps wrongly. Distractor 3 prepends ring (alphabetical operation). Distractor 4 prepends 36.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: If a machine reverses the order of items at every step, an input of 'A B C D E' becomes after Step II:
questions.explanation: Reversing an arrangement TWICE yields the original. Step I reverses 'A B C D E' → 'E D C B A'. Step II reverses again → 'A B C D E'. Distractor 1 is Step I result. Distractors 3, 4 are unrelated operations.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Input: 18 11 22 33 14 27. The machine moves all EVEN numbers to the left side and ODD to the right, preserving each side's order. Output:
questions.explanation: Evens in input order: 18, 22, 14. Odds in input order: 11, 33, 27. Output: 18 22 14 11 33 27. Distractor 1 puts odds first. Distractor 3 reverses internal order. Distractor 4 fully sorts.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Input: cat 5 dog 2 bird 8 fish 1. Step I moves the smallest number rightmost. After Step I:
questions.explanation: Smallest number is 1, already at the rightmost position → Step I leaves it unchanged. Step II would move next-smallest 2 to rightmost-but-one. Distractor 2 puts 1 leftmost. Distractor 3 partially sorts. Distractor 4 random.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: If a machine in each step swaps the first and last elements of the arrangement, after Step III the input 'P Q R S T' becomes:
questions.explanation: Step I swaps first and last: T Q R S P. Step II swaps again, restoring P Q R S T. Step III: T Q R S P (back to Step-I state). Pattern repeats every 2 steps; odd steps differ from even. Distractor 1 = Step II / Step IV. Distractors 3, 4 are different operations.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Input: 2 4 6 8 10. A machine adds 1 to each number per step. After Step IV the arrangement is:
questions.explanation: Each step adds 1 to every number. After 4 steps, each is +4. 2+4=6, 4+4=8, 6+4=10, 8+4=12, 10+4=14. Distractor 1 = Step I. Distractor 3 = Step III. Distractor 4 = Step VIII.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: When solving machine I-O sequences, the BEST first step is to:

options.option_text: Memorise common pattern templates from textbooks
Identify the rule by comparing two consecutive shown steps
Skip immediately to the last step asked in the question
Assume the rule is alphabetical sorting always

questions.explanation: Comparing two consecutive steps reveals which element moved and where → identify the rule. Then apply it forward / backward. Memorisation (distractor 1) doesn't help with novel rules. Skipping (distractor 3) loses the rule. Assuming alphabetical (distractor 4) is wrong if numbers are involved.
